name: Phantom Portals / XerXes Visual System
status: STYLE LOCK — use as implementation source of truth
palette_rule: Use only these five core colors. Create hierarchy with opacity, brightness, borders, gradients between core colors, and neutral transparency—not new accent hues.

typography.font_binary_note: Font binaries are intentionally not bundled. Antigravity may use locally installed/open-source fonts during development or fall back to the provided system stacks.

visual_identity.overall: Ultra-crisp technical, cinematic tactical, premium, highly readable
visual_identity.phantom_usage: Rare hero imagery; emblem/glyph is common, full character is reserved for landing/hero/portal moments
visual_identity.panel_material: Layered composite: near-black + graphite + metallic gold frame + controlled purple energy
visual_identity.panel_geometry: Mixed by importance; heavy tactical frame on hero/critical panels, restrained precision frame on utility panels
visual_identity.glow: Strong neon only on active/selected/hero states; normal states remain crisp and controlled
visual_identity.background: Subtle circuitry/grid, dark and low contrast
visual_identity.telemetry: Cinematic tactical but readable; data first, effects second
visual_identity.motion: Balanced; short feedback motion for normal navigation, cinematic motion reserved for major transitions
visual_identity.layout: Hybrid system: shared shell with flexible module-specific workspace
visual_identity.quotes: Maximum one quote/tagline, only in a bottom corner or footer; never repeat quotes across the interface.

content_rules: Never use decorative typography for body copy.
Avoid letterspacing on paragraphs and small labels.
Use all-caps sparingly for small UI labels only.
Keep body copy bright enough for immediate reading.
Do not let glow reduce text sharpness.
Do not turn every border into a neon element.
Do not invent extra operator colors beyond the five-color system.
Do not place large Phantom character art behind dense data panels.
Keep controls and information hierarchy more important than decoration.
